newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania fuel body blames port for dock delays.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania fuel body blames port for dock delays.

text.p: The state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) on Sunday blamed the Tanzania Harbours Authority (THA) for delays in offloading petroleum products in the capital's port.
TPDC said the mooring facility for oil tankers was out of action, causing congestion at Dar es Salaam port, leading to delays in delivery of fuel to consumers.
The statement, carried as a half-page announcement in local newspapers, said delays in delivery of fuel to retail outlets were beyond the TPDC's control.
Fire on December 25 destroyed the port's main oil discharging facility, which also handled oil supplies for landlocked Zambia and Malawi.
All crude oil and refined petroleum products are now being discharged at a smaller oil jetty, normally used solely for white oil products, and not for crude oil.
The TPDC said three bulk tankers were expected to arrive between Febuary 25 and March 7. Two other tankers are currently offloading.

Large tankers have to discharge offshore because the channel entrance to Dar es Salaam port is shallow and narrow. Until last December they were able to tie up at the floating mooring, but now they must transfer their cargo into smaller tankers which carry it into the main harbour.
To alleviate local fuel shortages, TPDC said super grade petrol destined for Malawi will be diverted to the Tanzanian market.
Public arguments between state bodies, waged in the form of announcements under bold headlines, are emerging as a Tanzanian phenomenon.

Last month President Benjamin Mkapa ordered state-owned Air Tanzania and the National Insurance Corporation to settle a dispute over insurance cover in private and not as a "press release war" in the nation's daily newspapers.
